Reverend may be so you could do like January 1 March 1 with the authorization wouldn’t expire.

items.text:
Good morning All
Since the very nature of PM&R is chronic pain. Do you find that your providers have a high rate of 99214 E/M? I often feel like I may be over-coding these services

Thanks !

topComments.text: Yes we often find based on AMA guidelines we are billing a large percentage of 99214 and even when we evaluate opportunities to buy other practices it’s much the same. There’s 3 categories and 2/3 need to meet moderate level decision making. Typically 2 chronic conditions and medications ordered gets you there but things like imaging review or orders and lab review counts as well. There’s a chart online from the AMA that makes it pretty reasonable to understand. But if you aren’t billing mostly 99214 I would think your providers are missing documentation.

I'm a Provider auditor-educator, I do find New Patient level 4s are more common in this specialty than others.  It's due to by the time they come to you, they've had several tests that need reviewed and usually have more than 1 chronic problem.  Established patients it's going to depend on your documentation.  A lot of these patients also have chronic illnesses that increase the risk of injections and such, but that has to be documented.

I apologize if this is a total newb question, but here goes--I shared a KZA Question/Answer w/ our providers that stated (in summary):

If a diagnostic ultrasound is performed at the same location, it’s included as part of any ultrasound-guided procedure performed there.  We can only bill for both if they are performed at separate anatomic locations.  
[https://www.kzanow.com/coding-coaches/diagnostic-ultrasound-followed-by-ultrasound-guided-injection-07-09-26](https://nam09.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.kzanow.com%2Fcoding-coaches%2Fdiagnostic-ultrasound-followed-by-ultrasound-guided-injection-07-09-26&data=05%7C02%7Cbbennett%40hdssbend.com%7C11e20c8bf0e74ad0a5f608dee208861c%7Cb7987c6eb293420cb13245de0fed4801%7C0%7C0%7C639196723445611331%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=38cx1%2B8YFaJFz9HMz8KJpLy2uGJQv1woqZhPu3R5zgY%3D&reserved=0)

One of our providers was not thrilled with this advice and stated, "This is not what we have been taught in training. A diagnostic procedure is specifically different from needle guidance. The needle guidance code has been greatly reduced from what it was initially in terms of RVU When they started doing the bundle joint injection. Would be interested to see what the ultrasound and imaging resources and groups say."

I was curious to hear this group's thoughts on this and his response to it.
items.previewTitle: Diagnostic Ultrasound Followed by Ultrasound Guided Injection — KZA
items.previewDescription: We have a Pain Interventionalist performing diagnostic MSK ultrasounds, followed by an ultrasound guided injection. We bill both codes but the claims keep bundling. Is there a way to avoid this?

topComments.text: I do a lot of ultrasound, both diagnostic and procedural, and never have been able to bill for diagnostic and procedural on the same day.

The article you linked matches my understanding as well. You can bill 76881 or 76882 if it was performed on a DIFFERENT body part from the ultrasound guided injection, but not if it was on the same body part. For example, billing 76881 for the RT knee and billing 20611 for the LT knee would be okay bc it's different body parts (different laterality). Or 76882 for the LT hand and 76942 + inj for the RT shoulder would be okay too. You would have to use 59 modifier in those cases to separate the two services. It would be more questionable if it's for the same body part because it is assumed that when you use US guidance for needle placement, you're already looking at/evaluating that body part during the guidance and so the US exam would be considered bundled/double dipping. Keep in mind that your payers may have guidelines about US exams that include frequency limitations too. My MAC has an LCD for US exams too. Be prepared to have to send documention to show that both an US exam and US guidance were done on the separate body parts (e.g. US images for both exam + needle guidance, US exam report).

items.text: Q:  is a UDS ORDER from a provider expected to be enough to support the lab service, or is the lab expected to make sure the pain mgt provider's services support the UDS order?  We're having a debate about how much the lab is on the hook for the medical necessity if the provider is properly submitting a lab order.

topComments.text:
The provider's order is the primary support for medical necessity — the lab is not required to audit the pain management provider's clinical records or second-guess the treating physician's judgment. CMS places medical necessity squarely on the ordering provider.

That said, the lab isn't completely off the hook. The lab's own independent duties are about process integrity, not clinical validation — things like correct coding, not auto-adding drug classes that weren't ordered, and not designing requisition forms that steer providers toward larger panels. Where labs get into trouble is when they see obvious red flags (e.g., 100% of patients getting definitive testing every single visit) and just keep processing without asking questions.

If you’re referring to CPT 80305 or 80307, the provider should document the medical necessity for the urine drug screen in the note. Documentation should include:

* Continuation of chronic pain medication/opioid therapy.
* A statement that a urine drug screen (UDS) was obtained/performed for medication compliance and monitoring.
* The appropriate diagnosis code supporting the test.

For patients on chronic opioid therapy, consider using Z79.891 – Long-term (current) use of opiate analgesic, as this is the diagnosis code specifically designated for long-term opioid use. Z79.899 Other long-term (current) drug therapy is more appropriate when the patient is on long-term medications that are not opioid analgesics. CMS includes Z79.891 as a covered diagnosis for urine drug testing in patients receiving chronic opioid therapy.

items.text:
I am seeking guidance on the appropriate CPT codes for anesthesia for the following interventional pain management procedures we perform. My understanding is that the anesthesia code selection is based on the patient's position during the procedure and whether the anesthesia services are provided by a separate anesthesia professional (anesthesiologist or CRNA).

Procedures:
* MBNB (Medial Branch Nerve Block)
* TF (Transforaminal Epidural Steroid Injection)
* RFA (Radiofrequency Ablation)
* LESI (Lumbar Epidural Steroid Injection)
* CESI (Cervical Epidural Steroid Injection)

Could you please advise on the correct CPT codes for anesthesia to be billed for these procedures?

topComments.text: You really need to look at the insurance policies and Medicare LCD because they will not cover Anesthesia or Mac anesthesia for several procedures now.

From my knowledge, the anesthesia codes depend on the procedure performed and the spinal region of the procedure.  These are the codes that I know of for when anesthesia is provided by a separate anesthesia provider (and is not the same provider that is performing the procedure):

MBNB, TF, ESIs:
01937 - Anesthesia for percutaneous image-guided injection, drainage or aspiration procedures on the spine or spinal cord; **cervical or thoracic**
01938 - Anesthesia for percutaneous image guided injection, drainage or aspiration procedures on the spine or spinal cord; **lumbar or sacral**

RFA:
01939 - Anesthesia for percutaneous image guided destruction procedures by neurolytic agent on the spine or spinal cord; **cervical or thoracic**
01940 - Anesthesia for percutaneous image guided destruction procedures by neurolytic agent on the spine or spinal cord; **lumbar or sacral**

items.text: I have a question what code everyone is using for ganglion impar blocks 64999, 64451 0r 64520. I am getting so much conflicting imformation regarding this procedure and just want some advice on it.

topComments.text: 64999 For Ganglion Impar. I believe there is a CPT assist with the guidance . I Really wish they would add a category 1 code for it though  .
I’ve used 64999 with description to Michigan Blue Cross/Blue shield and haven’t had a problem. I haven’t used it on any other carrier yet.
